what: 1. Simulate count data from a Poisson distribution
title: Session 4 lab exercise: Poisson log-linear regression
text: (example, number hospital visits persons 70 3-year period), : . 10,000 persons annotated “race” “white” “non-white” b. “white” persons average 3.5 hospital visits time period c. “non-white” persons average 3 hospital visits
code: library(tidyverse) ## ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ── ## ✔ dplyr     1.2.1     ✔ readr     2.2.0 ## ✔ forcats   1.0.1     ✔ stringr   1.6.0 ## ✔ ggplot2   4.0.3     ✔ tibble    3.3.1 ## ✔ lubridate 1.9.5     ✔ tidyr     1.3.2 ## ✔ purrr     1.2.2      ## ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ── ## ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter() ## ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag() ## ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors set.seed(1) N <- 10000 simdat <- data.frame(race = sample(c("white", "non-white"), N, replace = TRUE)) %>%   mutate(race = factor(race, levels = c("white", "non-white"))) %>%   mutate(y = rpois(N, lambda = ifelse(race == "white", 3.5, 3.0)))

what: 2. Fit a log-linear Poisson model of count outcomes
title: Session 4 lab exercise: Poisson log-linear regression
text: “race” predictor. Note, context tend use terms “predictor” “covariate” interchangeably, mean variable used predictor regression model.
code: fit <- glm(y ~ race, data = simdat, family = poisson(link = "log")) summary(fit) ##  ## Call: ## glm(formula = y ~ race, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = simdat) ##  ## Coefficients: ##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     ## (Intercept)    1.254710   0.007564  165.88   <2e-16 *** ## racenon-white -0.161428   0.011137  -14.49   <2e-16 *** ## --- ## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ##  ## (Dispersion parameter for poisson family taken to be 1) ##  ##     Null deviance: 11041  on 9999  degrees of freedom ## Residual deviance: 10831  on 9998  degrees of freedom ## AIC: 39419 ##  ## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 5

what: 3. Use a chi-square test on deviance residuals
title: Session 4 lab exercise: Poisson log-linear regression
text: test null hypothesis relationship mean hospital visits race. difference deviance residuals (11041 - 10831) = 210, difference 1 degrees freedom. critical threshold rejection p=0.05 : reject H0H_0 BEWARE MISSING DATA: SAFER

title: Session 4: loglinear regression part 1
text: Random component specifies conditional distribution response variable - doesn’t normal can distribution belongs “exponential” family distributions Systematic component specifies linear function predictors (linear predictor) Link [denoted g(.)] specifies relationship expected value random component systematic component, can linear nonlinear

title: Session 4: loglinear regression part 1
text: model: yi=E[y|x]+ϵi=β0+β1x1i+β2x2i+...+βpxpi+ϵiy_i = E[y|x] + \epsilon_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{1i} + \beta_2 x_{2i} + ... + \beta_p x_{pi} + \epsilon_i Random component yiy_i normally distributed: ϵi∼iidN(0,σϵ2)\epsilon_i \stackrel{iid}{\sim} N(0, \sigma_\epsilon^2) Systematic component (linear predictor): β0+β1x1i+β2x2i+...+βpxpi\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{1i} + \beta_2 x_{2i} + ... + \beta_p x_{pi} Link function identity link: g(E(y|x))=E(y|x)g(E(y | x)) = E(y | x). modeling mean directly, transformation.

title: Session 4: loglinear regression part 1
text: model: Logit(P(x))=log(P(x)1−P(x))=β0+β1x1i+β2x2i+...+βpxpi Logit(P(x)) = log \left( \frac{P(x)}{1-P(x)} \right) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{1i} + \beta_2 x_{2i} + ... + \beta_p x_{pi} Random component: yiy_i follows Binomial distribution (outcome binary variable) Systematic component: linear predictor β0+β1x1i+β2x2i+...+βpxpi \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{1i} + \beta_2 x_{2i} + ... + \beta_p x_{pi} Link function: logit (Converts Prob -> log-odds) g(P(x))=logit(P(x))=log(P(x)1−P(x)) g(P(x)) = logit(P(x)) = log\left( \frac{P(x)}{1-P(x)} \right) P(x)=g−1(β0+β1x1i+β2x2i+...+βpxpi) P(x) = g^{-1}\left( \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{1i} + \beta_2 x_{2i} + ... + \beta_p x_{pi}  \right)

title: Session 4: loglinear regression part 1
text: log(E[Yi])=β0+β1RACEi+β2TRTi+β3ALCHi+β4DRUGi log(E[Y_i]) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \textrm{RACE}_i + \beta_2 \textrm{TRT}_i + \beta_3 \textrm{ALCH}_i + \beta_4 \textrm{DRUG}_i  equivalently: E[Yi]=exp(β0+β1RACEi+β2TRTi+β3ALCHi+β4DRUGi) E[Y_i] = exp \left( \beta_0 + \beta_1 \textrm{RACE}_i + \beta_2 \textrm{TRT}_i + \beta_3 \textrm{ALCH}_i + \beta_4 \textrm{DRUG}_i \right)  E[Yi]E[Y_i] expected number emergency room visits patient . Important note: Modeling log(E[Yi])log(E[Y_i]) equivalent modeling E(log(Yi))E(log(Y_i))

title: Session 4: loglinear regression part 1
text: Instead, model mean count per unit time: log(E[Yi]/ti)=β0+β1RACEi+β2TRTi+β3ALCHi+β4DRUGi \begin{aligned} log(E[Y_i]/t_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \textrm{RACE}_i + \beta_2 \textrm{TRT}_i +  \beta_3 \textrm{ALCH}_i + \nonumber \\ \beta_4 \textrm{DRUG}_i \end{aligned} equivalently: log(E[Yi])=β0+β1RACEi+β2TRTi+β3ALCHi+β4DRUGi+log(ti) \begin{aligned} log(E[Y_i]) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \textrm{RACE}_i + \beta_2 \textrm{TRT}_i +  \beta_3 \textrm{ALCH}_i + \nonumber \\ \beta_4 \textrm{DRUG}_i + log(t_i) \end{aligned} log(ti)log(t_i) covariate, called offset

title: Session 4: loglinear regression part 1
text: Model number counts per unit time Poisson-distributed + expected number counts per time λi\lambda_i E[Yi]/ti=λiE[Y_i]/t_i = \lambda_ilog(E[Yi]/ti)=log(λi)log(E[Y_i]/t_i) = log(\lambda_i)log(E[Yi])=log(λi)+log(ti)log(E[Y_i]) = log(\lambda_i) + log(t_i) Recalling log-linear model systematic component: log(E[Yi])=β0+β1RACEi+β2TRTi+β3ALCHi+β4DRUGi+log(ti) \begin{aligned} log(E[Y_i]) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \textrm{RACE}_i + \beta_2 \textrm{TRT}_i +  \beta_3 \textrm{ALCH}_i + \nonumber \\ \beta_4 \textrm{DRUG}_i + log(t_i) \end{aligned}
